propositions: A context-limit escalation in Pass-1 finder silently substitutes a Bedrock-qualified model with a bare Anthropic model id, bypassing the model-class table and causing provider mismatch errors or unbudgeted spend.

The _rung_target function compares rung-derived provider forms without considering the run's actual configured model, causing the equality check to always hold when the class table is unconfigured, degrading to bare Anthropic family names.

When cfg.model is Bedrock-qualified and no class table is configured, the escalation targets become bare Anthropic ids, leaving cfg.model_provider untouched and composing invalid Bedrock model ids like 'bedrock:claude-opus-4-8'.
The one-criterion retry substitution occurs on the entry rung with frontier model before any deep escalation is needed, not confined to rare cases, affecting common retry paths.

The fix threads the run's primary model into _rung_target and applies provider-agreement logic: preserve the primary model verbatim on its own rung when providers differ, or drop the rung if providers differ on higher rungs where the target cannot be named in the run's provider.
